note: Newest first. One entry per thing a player would notice. Dates are the day it went live.

entries.title: The house has a soundtrack, and Lucy has a voice
entries.body: Nocturnal Drift plays in the house, looped with a crossfade so there is never a gap, and it remembers if you turn it off. Lucy's voice is a real ferret: one recording, cut into seventeen whole phrases. The sim decides when she makes a noise and which one, so a seed replays her voice too. Zoomies are loud. A sulking Lucy says nothing at all.
entries.note: Lucy's voice: "Ferret" by J. Zazvurek, CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: Inspect her hoard
entries.body: The end-of-run card has a second face: everything she has ever stolen, oldest first, each with what she thought about it. Shoe is nice. My shoe. The thoughts come from what actually happened when she took it, never invented. Things the house tidied away stay on the list, crossed out, because she remembers. The eye lives here now.

entries.title: She carries what she steals, and she is not always proud
entries.body: Stolen things used to vanish the moment she grabbed them. Now they ride along in her mouth to the couch. And the end-of-run portrait was showing proud about three runs in four; pride is now for firsts, so her real moods finally show.

entries.title: Show the working
entries.body: A small eye on the end-of-run card opens the arithmetic: the world seed, how many decisions she made, her last decision with the three things she nearly did instead and their real odds, every action with the reason the sim recorded, and a replay string. Proof there is no AI in here — seeded dice and tag weights, and you can reconstruct the run exactly. It only appears after the door closes, so it can never be used to steer one.

entries.note: A real run. The sock appears five times because its fabric weighting bent what she noticed all day — that is the mood system visible in the log.

entries.title: Lucy is playable
entries.body: Pack her cage, open the door, and get out of the way. She explores seven rooms, steals things, sulks, naps on your laundry, and builds a hoard under the couch that persists between runs. Every run ends with what she did and what she learned. One seed, no sound yet, sprites still rough — but it is a real game now, not a page.

entries.title: The game explains itself
entries.body: A how-it-works card on your first world, and a HOW TO PLAY button after that. The important part, which everybody misses: the order buttons are a shortcut, not the rules. You can type anything you can describe and it becomes a real order with a real price and a real roll.

entries.title: About, Contact, and a nav that fits
entries.body: The nav is four things now. There is a page about what this actually is, and a contact form that reaches a person — with a list of excellent reasons to write and a few reasons not to. The ferret is unavailable and uninterested.

entries.title: The narrator narrates again
entries.body: Briefings were reciting dice — "rolling a 4, drift neutral" — and flattening big ideas into menu orders. Now the arithmetic stays on the board and the prose tells you what it meant. Say you are a pacifist society that sells flattering sketches and the world remembers it, prices it as its own scheme, and the neighbours form opinions. The end-of-world chronicle opens on what happened while you were not looking.

entries.title: Playable in a browser
entries.body: The world you could only run inside Claude Code now runs at unstuck-games.com/elsewhere/play — password-gated while it is early. Python still rolls the dice; three small models do the talking.

entries.title: A home of our own
entries.body: Every game moved to unstuck-games.com, off a borrowed address and onto a machine we run. Any game now opens the studio picker, so you are never stranded on a page with no way back to the rest.

entries.title: God Mode: one ad a day, hours on tap
entries.body: One ad per game per day. After that, switch God Mode on for an hour whenever you like until tomorrow, free. No second ad, no chain, no energy, no currency. Surely you have to watch another one? No. Go play.

entries.title: Lucy has a page, and a newsletter
entries.body: A launcher game about a long animal, except you do not aim her. One email when the door opens.
